verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.4 'Without JavaScript' (no [D] mark): 'Controls are rendered with the disabled attribute, which the island removes when it hydrates, so a control never looks usable before it is.' This sentence supports the finding's expected. 4.0 [D] 'Controls are present but disabled until the island has hydrated' only adds the attribute and does not permit a look that seems usable.
verdicts.evidence: Read at b9b8504 (worktree detached there and clean). ToolFrame.svelte:269-282: .control sets color var(--text), background var(--page), border 1px solid var(--text) and cursor pointer, and .control:disabled sets only 'cursor: default'. The same pattern is in History.svelte:76-90, Predict.svelte:167-170, T01:770, T04:508, T05:1056, T06:545, T07:666, T08:716, T09:736, T10:1413, T11:641 (.tab), T15:807, T16:661, BoardEditor:576, t15/Tabs, t15/ConventionSwitch and t08/WeylGraph. Board.svelte:276 changes only the cursor of .hit. No file in site/src/styles or site/src/layouts has a disabled rule. Only Nav.astro's .theme-switch:disabled adds opacity 0.6. Board.svelte:184-193 with Node.svelte:30-31: before hydration a node that can act is disabled but still draws the second ring that 6.3 uses for 'may act here'. Records searched: DECISIONS.md and every decisions/*.md, including P0-A5 (disc, ring and cursor styles, with no rule for disabled), P1-A2 (fieldset disabled until hydration, nothing on its look) and P1-A5. None records a choice to style disabled controls like enabled ones. Grep for 'usable|not-allowed|opacity|disabled look' found nothing relevant. round1-confirmed-A/B, round1-deferred and RESULTS.md hold no finding on the disabled look. reports/gate-G4.md (it names b9b8504 as the gate commit) has no open item on it. 8.3 [D] 'Calm, bright, low-chrome' says nothing about the disabled state. incidental: none.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed: no sentence permits a disabled control that looks enabled, and 7.4 states the opposite in words, while the cursor change shows only on hover with a pointer; R2 failed: the expected matches 7.4's 'never looks usable before it is'. The finding stretches the claim to frozen boards after hydration, which 7.4's sentence (about the time before hydration) covers only loosely, and CONTRACTS 5.1 asks only for the attribute, but the cause before hydration stands on 7.4 alone; R3 failed: ToolFrame and History are phase 0 and 1, and T10 and T11 are phase 4, at gate G4; R4 not applicable, since no oracle quantity is involved; R5 failed: 7.4 carries no [D], 4.0 [D] does not cover the look, and no D-number, owner answer or decisions entry records the styling; R6 failed: no earlier record of this cause. Major fits the rubric ('a behaviour the specification states is missing or wrong').

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.4: 'Tools that draw on a canvas (T10, and T8 above 192 elements) ship an SVG snapshot of their default view' and 'A Playwright run with JavaScript disabled checks, for every lesson, that the text, every default figure and every table are present'; SPEC 4 T10 (phase 4): 'Without JavaScript the default projection is shown as an SVG image produced at build time'; RED-TEAM-COMMON 2 'a test that would pass against an empty function'. These passages support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read site/tests/e2e/nojs.spec.ts:60-124 at b9b8504. toolReport takes boards ([data-board-group] with [data-node] beside an svg with content) before drawings ([role=img] with children and a name). Its only filter is outside(details, noscript), with no visibility test, and figureProblems checks only kind, text alternative and node values. T10GeometryStudio.svelte:964-982: the ring Board, and also '<div class="drawing" role="img" aria-label hidden={!drawnOnce}><canvas>', which is hidden in the server markup and still satisfies the drawing branch. The snapshot (data-out="snapshot") is never required to hold a point. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity.md 'the default figure of the run without JavaScript' records this predicate. It is a builder's record (no [D], no section 10 default, no owner answer), it does not say that T10's ring board counts as its figure, and it does not address hidden elements. The regression test of P3-RT-06-03 (nojs.spec.ts:271-299) covers only tools/board/ and modules/m0-start/. Partial correction to the finding: other specs do count snapshot points. T10.spec.ts:397-417 checks the circles and segments of the tool route against wythoff A3 (1,0,1), and M7.spec.ts:325-348 counts circles for b8 (E8) and also for b9 and b3 (D4), not only b8 as the finding says. So a blank snapshot passes every check on the other 10 M7 instances, not on all 14. The cause, a figure predicate that never reads T10's snapshot, stands. reports/gate-G4.md records the nojs run as passing, with no open item on this.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed: 7.4 asks the run to check that every default figure is present, and the round 1 precedent P3-RT-06-03 (confirmed and fixed) treats an accepted blank figure as a defect; R2 failed: the finding reads 7.4 and T10 correctly, and its only overstatement (M7.spec counts b3 and b9 as well as b8, and T10.spec covers the tool route) narrows the affected instances without removing the cause; R3 failed: T10 is phase 4 at gate G4; R4 not applicable; R5 failed: RT-FIX-P3-test-integrity is a builder's record, not a [D] choice, section 10 default or owner answer, and it does not cover T10's snapshot or hidden elements; R6 failed: there is no record of this case, and the P3-RT-06-03 regression test covers other routes. Minor fits the rubric ('a test that could be stronger without being wrong'), since the snapshots are correct at the gate.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 4.0 'Works before and without JavaScript' ('The default state of every tool is rendered to HTML and SVG at build time'); 8.1 P1 ('The page works with no interaction at all ... Each tool has a meaningful starting state'); decisions/RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4.md, 'data-measured marks an output that measures the reader's machine (P4-MERGE-04)'. The decision covers only the measured element and does not mention the words around it.
verdicts.evidence: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1024-1029 at b9b8504: 'Drawn: {pointsDrawn ?? ssr.points} points, ... edges, in {drawMs === null ? '' : ...} ms; edits: ...'. In server markup drawMs is null, so the line reads 'Drawn: N points, M edges, in ms'. The fragment RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4 says: 'It is not part of any default state: the server markup renders the element empty and the hydrated tool fills it'. That records the empty element but not a sentence that keeps 'in' and 'ms' around it. DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: red-team round 1, group B and the deferred round' records P4-MERGE-04 as fixed ('drawMs is marked as a measured output') and does not accept the dangling clause. P4-A3's T10 entries do not record this line's wording. SPEC 7.6 [D] asks a browser test to record the drawing time and does not require the time to be shown in the tool, so the line is the builder's own text, and 8.4 and 4.0 give no permission for a clause with no number. The finding's 'reads as a complete state' is its own paraphrase of 8.1 P1, not a quotation.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed: no sentence permits a shown clause with no value, and the decision permits only the empty element; R2 only partial: the expected paraphrases 8.1 P1 loosely, but the cause the finding names (the words 'in' and 'ms' outside the measured element) is not a misreading of the decision, which is silent on them; R3 failed: T10 is phase 4 at gate G4; R4 not applicable; R5 failed: RT-FIX-P3-nojs-phase4 is a builder's record that covers the element, not the sentence, and there is no [D], D-number or owner answer; R6 failed: P4-MERGE-04 is recorded as fixed, and this is a new effect around that fix. Minor fits the rubric ('wording').
